title: The Hypercontext Protocol
logline: A person keeps their whole context, everything about their life a machine could know, inside one walled castle they own: rooms they designed, one gate they control, and a sealed keep at the center that never opens. Services that want to serve them do not get the castle; the gatekeeper passes out a single labeled sliver, carried on a thin beam, exactly enough for excellence of service and nothing more. The thesis is the social contract itself: share for relevance, never beyond excellence of service.
refrain: Share for relevance, never beyond excellence of service.
